Non-vacuity check on the get-only round-trip: the candidate is asserted populated immediately after JsonDefaults.Options deserialization, before the save, so a reverted get-only property would fail at that assertion.

Non-vacuity check on activation/secret rotation: verified ConfigurationSnapshotService.TryReplace rebuilds the secret map from the candidate and TryAcquire gates on the exact version, so the version-2 new-secret match and version-1 old-secret rejection are real, not incidental.

Non-vacuity check on the invalid-save persistence assertion: the initial and rejected payloads differ in WebhookSecret/BaseUrl/EnabledLibraries, so reading the persisted file after the rejected save genuinely detects persistence.

Non-vacuity check on the re-render: confirmed the default Quality template is '{value}' versus the saved 'Q{value}', so the renderer configuration fingerprint and the desired publication fingerprint actually change; the last RenderRequest also carries the new BadgeDefinitions.
